neighbours.label: relocation or life-decision verb in a biographical narrative (moved to, decided to)
fire: After graduating from college in 1902, she moved to Boston to teach.

In 1850 the family moved west to Oregon in a covered wagon.
When the war ended, he decided to study medicine in Vienna.
Unable to find work, they moved to Detroit in search of jobs.
At the age of forty, she decided to become a painter.
Shortly after the wedding, the pair moved to London.
quiet: After graduating from college in 1902, she taught in Boston for years.
Tired of city life, the couple spent weekends on a farm in Vermont.
Following his defeat, the senator gave a short speech to supporters.
In 1850 the family lived in Oregon in a small cabin.
When the war ended, he was studying medicine in Vienna.
Unable to find work, they spent the winter in Detroit.
